channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Construction Company Fined 200,000 Som for Violations in Kara-Suu
item.description: In the Kara-Suu district of Osh region, the owner of a construction materials plant was fined 200,000 som for violations. The Ministry of Construction reported that inspections revealed deviations from design solutions and incomplete documentation. The owner was issued a directive to rectify the identified issues.

item.title: AI Identifies 44 Errors in Russian Version of Kyrgyzstan's Constitution
item.description: Member of Parliament Dastan Bekeshev announced that artificial intelligence detected 44 errors and inaccuracies in the Russian translation of Kyrgyzstan's Constitution. He cautioned that the analysis was based on texts from the Ministry of Justice website and may not reflect the official original document. The errors relate to meaning, interpretation, and translation quality.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Open 189 Day Care Units for Children with Autism
item.description: Kazakhstan is expanding its mental health support system by opening 189 day care units for children with autism and 81 mental health centers. This initiative is part of a comprehensive plan for population mental health protection from 2027-2031. The goal is to ensure accessible specialized care across all regions and address the shortage of specialists.

item.title: Former Emergency Situations Minister's Daughter Seeks Funding for Hydroelectric Plant Construction
item.description: Osiris Energo company has applied to the Development Bank of Kazakhstan for financing the construction of a small hydroelectric power plant on the Shelek River in the Almaty region. Galia Zhumanazarova, daughter of the former head of the Ministry of Emergency Situations, is the beneficiary. The project is currently in the second stage of expert review.

item.title: Illegal Activities of 'Albi' Pawnshop Network Uncovered, Earning Over 146 Million Tenge
item.description: The Financial Monitoring Agency's Almaty region department has stopped the illegal activities of the 'Albi' pawnshop network. Despite being removed from the microfinance registry, the company continued to issue loans secured by jewelry in Almaty and Turkestan regions, charging 2% daily interest, over six times the legal limit.

item.title: France: Macron Rejects Interior Minister's Resignation Amid Widespread Protests
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron has rejected the resignation request of Interior Minister Gérald Darmanin following widespread unrest. The Elysée Palace stated the decision was necessary for continuous leadership of public order forces. Macron acknowledged shortcomings in assessment and intelligence that led to riots, building damage, and looting.

item.title: Kazakhstan Cracks Down on Pawnshop Network with Illegal Income Exceeding 146 Million Tenge
item.description: Kazakhstan's Financial Monitoring Agency has shut down an illegal pawnshop network that continued lending after losing its license. The network, operating in Almaty and Turkestan regions, issued loans secured by jewelry at a daily interest rate of 2%, significantly exceeding the legal limit. The illicit income surpassed 146 million tenge.

item.title: Kazakh Gymnasts Reach World Championship Finals in Artistic and All-Around Events
item.description: Kazakhstan's gymnasts Nariman Kurbanov and Nurtan Idrisov have qualified for the World Championships finals in Rotterdam. Kurbanov advanced to the pommel horse final, securing second place in qualification. Idrisov qualified for the individual all-around final, finishing 17th. The men's team did not qualify for the team final, missing out on an Olympic quota.

item.title: US Secretary of State Antony Blinken Praises Uzbekistan's Role in Central Asia
item.description: US Secretary of State Antony Blinken highlighted Uzbekistan's pivotal role in Central Asia during his visit, calling the country the region's foundation. He anticipates that agreements worth billions of dollars will be signed, underscoring the strategic importance of Uzbekistan's position and engagement in regional processes.

item.title: Kyrgyz Parliamentarian Criticizes Project Implementation Unit Spending of Millions
item.description: A Member of Parliament in Kyrgyzstan has criticized the significant spending by Project Implementation Units (PIUs), funded by international loans and grants. The lawmaker questioned the effectiveness of allocating 10% of project funds to PIUs, citing a lack of results despite substantial financial allocations for projects like the "Chet-Kairyk" canal.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee Uncovers International Online Fraud Scheme
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee (KNB) has exposed an international online fraud scheme organized by Chinese citizens. Thirteen Chinese nationals were expelled from the country after being found to be in violation of immigration laws and operating a clandestine fraud network. They possessed significant computer equipment, phones, Starlink systems, and cryptocurrency.

item.title: Qatar and UAE Foreign Ministers Discuss Regional Stability and Bilateral Cooperation
item.description: Qatar's Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani, held a phone call with the UAE's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan. The discussion focused on strengthening bilateral cooperation and addressing regional issues, including recent developments and past disagreements between the two nations.

item.title: Kazakhstan Implements New Constitutional Principles for Political Modernization
item.description: Kazakhstan's new constitution, effective July 1, introduces significant reforms to modernize the political system and expand citizen participation. Key changes include the introduction of a Vice President role, defining the powers of the new legislative body, the Kurultai, and establishing the People's Council of Kazakhstan. These reforms aim to strengthen parliamentary oversight and improve feedback mechanisms.

item.title: Almaty Residents Resist Seizure of Garages for Akimat Parking Near Airport
item.description: Residents in Almaty's Turkistan district are protesting the seizure of their garages for state-owned parking. They claim the compensation offered is half the market value and that the garages are essential for storing bicycles and skis. Concerns are raised that the parking facility is not a defined public need and may be intended for taxi services.

item.title: Afghanistan-Pakistan Trade Declines Sharply by 74% Amid Border Disruptions
item.description: Trade between Afghanistan and Pakistan plummeted by 74% in the 2025-26 financial year, falling to $358 million from $1.3 billion, according to Pakistan’s Trade Development Authority. Prolonged border closures and heightened tensions at crossings like Torkham and Chaman significantly disrupted commercial activity, impacting traders and transport companies.

item.title: Kazakhstan Health Ministry Assesses Low Monkeypox Risk, Urges Precautions
item.description: Kazakhstan's Health Ministry assesses the risk of monkeypox spread as low but acknowledges potential importation. Comprehensive preventive measures are in place at border crossings, including enhanced monitoring. Citizens are advised to avoid close contact with individuals showing unexplained rashes and maintain personal hygiene.

item.title: Pawnshops Issued Loans at Illegal Interest Rates, Six Times Above Legal Limit
item.description: Authorities in two regions have shut down a network of pawnshops operating under the name "Albi-KM" for issuing loans at interest rates exceeding the legal limit by over six times. The pawnshops, previously excluded from microfinance activities, charged 2% daily interest. The criminal profit exceeded 146 million tenge.

item.title: Putin Proposes Trilateral Meeting with US and China to Discuss Ukraine Conflict
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin has proposed a trilateral summit with US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping to discuss the resolution of the Ukraine conflict. The meeting is suggested to take place during the APEC summit in November. While Trump may be receptive, a final decision has not yet been made.

item.title: Tajikistan Presents Initiatives on Water, Environment, and Peace at OIC Meeting
item.description: Tajikistan's Deputy Foreign Minister presented the country's position on current agenda issues at the 52nd session of the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers in Baghdad. He urged OIC member states to cooperate on implementing Tajikistan's international initiatives concerning water resources, environmental protection, and peace for future generations.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ministry of Health Monitors Monkeypox Risk Amid Global Cases
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Health is actively monitoring the epidemiological situation regarding monkeypox. While acknowledging the potential for the virus to reach the country due to international travel, the ministry stated that the risk of widespread transmission within Kazakhstan is low, considering the pathogen's transmission characteristics. Border controls have been intensified to prevent its entry.

item.title: Uzbekistan Joins Artemis Accords for Peaceful Exploration of Outer Space
item.description: Uzbekistan has become the 77th signatory to the Artemis Accords, which outline principles for peaceful, safe, and responsible space exploration. Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov signed the agreement in Samarkand. The US State Department noted discussions on strengthening strategic partnership, space cooperation, and opportunities for American companies in Uzbekistan's growing space sector.

item.title: China Hosts APEC Year, Driving Regional Cooperation and Shared Prosperity
item.description: China is hosting the APEC year, marked by over 300 events across more than 10 cities, focusing on building an Asia-Pacific community and promoting shared prosperity. Key priorities include openness, innovation, and cooperation. Meetings of senior officials have set the agenda for regional collaboration, with outcomes being detailed for the leaders' meeting.

item.title: Tajikistan-China Trade Exceeds $2.5 Billion in Eight Months
item.description: Tajikistan's trade turnover with China surpassed $2.5 billion in January-August 2026. Tajik President Emomali Rahmon met with Chinese Premier Li Qiang in Dushanbe to discuss strengthening economic cooperation. Both sides expressed readiness to support joint projects in industry, energy, transport, and agriculture.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan MP Demands Increased Oversight of ARIS Agency's Project Execution
item.description: A Member of the Kyrgyz Parliament, Alisher Kozuev, has called for enhanced control over the activities of the ARIS agency. He cited numerous complaints from regions regarding project delays despite timely funding. Kozuev urged the Ministry of Water Resources to strengthen supervision and evaluate ARIS's performance, particularly concerning water supply projects.

item.title: Thirteen Chinese Citizens Detained in Kazakhstan for International Online Fraud Scheme
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee has detained 13 Chinese citizens suspected of operating an international online fraud scheme. The individuals were found to be in violation of the country's laws. Authorities seized computer equipment, Starlink devices, and cryptocurrency, indicating the operation was coordinated from abroad.

item.title: US Secretary of State: US and Central Asian nations may sign multi-billion dollar deals
item.description: US Secretary of State Antony Blinken, visiting Samarkand, stated that representatives from nearly 300 American companies are present, indicating potential for multi-billion dollar deals beneficial to both the region and the United States. He expressed the US's desire to be a reliable partner for Central Asia, particularly Uzbekistan.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Only 415 out of 715 planned villages provided with drinking water in six years
item.description: A six-year program aimed to supply drinking water to 715 villages in Kyrgyzstan, but only 415 have been provided with access. A parliamentary committee was informed that the program, intended for 2020-2026, faced delays due to the COVID-19 pandemic and rising material costs. A new program for 2026-2030 is under consideration.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Criminal case opened against former teacher for beating children
item.description: A criminal case has been initiated against a former teacher in the Almaty region of Kazakhstan for physically assaulting children during religious education classes. The incident, which occurred in June 2026, gained public attention after a video circulated online. The teacher was dismissed, and the Spiritual Administration of Muslims of Kazakhstan stated parents had no claims.

item.title: Kazakhstan Strengthens Border Sanitary Control Amidst Global Monkeypox Concerns
item.description: Kazakhstan has intensified sanitary and quarantine control at its borders due to the global spread of monkeypox. The Ministry of Health reported that comprehensive preventive measures are being implemented, including enhanced checks at border crossings and monitoring of travelers from affected countries. All checkpoints are equipped with non-contact thermometers.

item.title: Chinese Citizens Detained in Kazakhstan for Operating Internet Fraud Scheme, Says KNB
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee (KNB) reported the detention of 13 Chinese citizens for violating immigration laws. During the investigation, it was discovered that they had established a clandestine international internet fraud scheme within Kazakhstan, targeting citizens of other countries. The KNB is continuing its efforts against illegal migration.

item.title: Trial Begins for Sanjar Bokayev: Allegations of Provocation, Secret Filming, and Witness Detainment
item.description: The trial of Kazakh activist and politician Sanjar Bokayev has commenced in Almaty, facing charges including fraud, theft, money laundering, spreading false information, and illegal logging. Bokayev denies all accusations, claiming they are fabricated. His defense argues for the innocence of all defendants, citing issues like lack of materials and the detention of a key witness.

item.title: Afghan Migrants in Italy Face Uncertainty in Residency and Exploitation in Work, Analyst Network Reports
item.description: Afghan migrants in Italy are reportedly facing precarious residency status and workplace exploitation, according to the Afghanistan Analysts Network. The report highlights the challenges these individuals encounter in securing stable living conditions and fair employment opportunities within Italy, indicating a significant humanitarian concern.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Fund could reach $100 billion by 2030
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Fund could potentially reach $100 billion by 2030, according to analyst Askhat Mukhtaruly. He suggests that revenues from production sharing agreements (PSAs) could be a key factor. While historical growth has been slower, future PSA terms might increase Kazakhstan's share, boosting the fund's assets.

item.title: Heating Tariffs to Be Reduced by 72% in Akmola Region Village
item.description: Heating and drinking water tariffs for residents and organizations in parts of Zerendinsky district will be lowered starting November 1, according to the Akmola region prosecutor's office. An enterprise was fined for including unjustified expenses in its tariff calculations.

item.title: Astana Construction Sites Record 78 Violations per 100 Inspections; Almaty Has 61
item.description: Construction sites in Astana reported 78 violations for every 100 control measures conducted. In Almaty, 61 violations were recorded during the same number of inspections, indicating significant regulatory issues in both major cities.

item.title: Tajikistan's Mufti Urges Migrants in Russia to Support Families and Each Other
item.description: Tajikistan's Mufti Saidmukarram Abdukodirzoda called on Tajik labor migrants in Russia to support each other, maintain unity, and focus on their families. He emphasized the importance of moral principles, respecting elders, and staying connected with children while abroad.

item.title: 51.4 km Road to be Built Along Rogun Dam Reservoir's Left Bank
item.description: A 51.4-kilometer road will be constructed along the left bank of the Rogun Hydropower Plant's reservoir, specifically between Sayidon and Labijar. The contract for this project has been signed. The plan includes 40.8 km of main road and 10.6 km of access roads, with completion expected in three years. Funding will be provided by the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank.

item.title: Iranian and Egyptian Foreign Ministers Discuss Regional Developments and Tensions
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty held a phone call to discuss regional developments, focusing on diplomatic efforts to reduce tensions and maintain stability. Araghchi also discussed regional issues with his Pakistani counterpart. These talks occur amidst heightened regional tensions involving Iran and the United States.

item.title: New UN Afghanistan Envoy Rabab Fatima Arrives in Kabul to Lead UNAMA Mission
item.description: Rabab Fatima, the UN secretary-general’s special representative for Afghanistan, has arrived in Kabul to formally begin her work leading the United Nations Assistance Mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA). She assumed leadership on Saturday and met with Taliban Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi. Fatima's appointment fills a vacancy after over a year without a permanent chief.

item.title: US Secretary of State Holds Meetings with Central Asian Foreign Ministers in Samarkand
item.description: US Secretary of State Antony Blinken is holding meetings with the foreign ministers of Central Asian countries in Samarkand on October 19. He met with Uzbekistan's Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov and plans to meet with Kazakhstan's Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi. A C5+1 meeting with all five Central Asian foreign ministers is scheduled, followed by a potential meeting with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev.
